7ef2738a018c93e352f5f06048bc248cd7940819.summary: Cylance report on a campaign it calls The Deception Project, which it says appeared to target Japanese companies and individuals from around August 2016. Attacks used spear phishing with LNK and PowerShell droppers, and the Ham and Tofu backdoors. Cylance tracks the group as Snake Wine. Samples were signed with a leaked Hacking Team certificate, which the report says may be an attempt to throw off attribution. Some infrastructure overlaps with MenuPass domains, but Cylance says it does not believe this is probable MenuPass activity.

hedges: Cylance believes some of the steps taken by the attacker could possibly be an attempt at a larger disinformation campaign.
Why the attackers chose to use this expired certificate to sign their malware samples is unknown.
The malware was likely done purely as an attempt to throw off attribution.
Cylance does not believe the MenuPass scenario to be probable, as a significant amount of time has elapsed between the activity sets.
